title: cross-tenant-trace-correlation-proxy-with-tempo-jaeger-compat-and-throttled-archive-fallback
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a lightweight, per-edge proxy that (1) correlates and normalizes incoming OTLP/Jaeger spans across tenant boundaries, (2) enriches spans with tenant metadata and routing hints, and (3) provides a throttled fallback path that writes hardened envelopes to an S3-backed archival queue when downstream Tempo/Jaeger sinks are overloaded. The proxy must preserve compatibility with existing Jaeger/Tempo ingestion semantics, avoid changing trace IDs for customer diagnostics, and support trace rehydration for backfill flows.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OTLP gRPC and Jaeger thrift/http formats and routes to Tempo and Jaeger backends based on tenant routing rules.
End-to-end passthrough p99 latency added by proxy < 50ms at steady state for typical span sizes (<=1KB).
Under simulated downstream overload (spike 3x baseline), proxy routes excess envelopes to S3 archive with <= 0.5% span loss and preserves ordering within tenant windows.
Trace correlation metadata (tenant_id, environment, cluster) present on root spans and searchable in Tempo within 5 minutes of ingestion in staging.
Automated e2e tests and contract tests added to trace-integrations CI; no regressions for Jaeger v1/v2 clients and OTLP-collector clients.
design_notes: Architecture: lightweight ingress proxy (go) with a small in-memory per-tenant buffer, a per-tenant rate-window, and a pluggable sink router (tempo/jaeger/s3).

Normalization: translate Jaeger tags to OTEL attributes, canonicalize timestamp nanoseconds, add tenant hint header and preserve original trace/span IDs in a span.checksum attribute for dedupe and rehydration.

Backpressure strategy: token-bucket per-tenant; when bucket exhausted, route to archival writer which batches to S3 with 60s max hold and per-tenant sharded prefix. Implement exponential backoff to sink retries and a circuit-breaker that triggers archive-only mode for a tenant.
Security: sign archival envelopes with KMS-backed key; include minimal PII scrubbing (configurable redaction rules).

Observability: expose /metrics (Prometheus), /health and a /debug/tenant-stats endpoint; emit internal spans to the control-plane collector under a separate service.name to avoid self-instrumentation loops.
implementation_plan: Week 1: build core OTLP gRPC and Jaeger thrift/http ingest adapters, unit tests for format translation.
Week 2: implement per-tenant routing, token-bucket limiter and archival writer library with S3 multipart support.
Week 3: integrate signature/KMS envelope signing, add config for redaction and sampling hints, prepare canary deploy manifests.
Week 4: run perf harness (benchmarks for 1K/5K/10K spans/s), iterate on memory and GC settings, add contract tests vs Tempo/Jaeger staging clusters.
Week 5: rollout canary (1% traffic -> 10% -> 50%), monitor key metrics, enable auto-fallback thresholds and finalize runbook.
testing_notes: Unit: format translation, tenant header propagation, checksum generation/dedup logic.
Integration: spin up Tempo and Jaeger test clusters in staging, verify searchability and latency under normal and spike loads.
Chaos: simulate sink outages and network partitions; verify archive path ingestion and eventual re-ingest to Tempo once sink recovers.
Load: use existing trace-hammer to validate p99 latency and throughput; baseline target 10k spans/s per proxy with < 8GB heap.
rollout_plan: Create Helm chart with feature flags: 'archiveFallback' and 'tenantNormalization'.
Deploy canary to edge cluster in us-east-1 (ingest mirror route) and validate with synthetic traces and real traffic mirrors.

Gradually increase mirror percentage; after 72h and no QoS regressions, switch 1% production traffic to proxy, increase to 10% after 48h, and expand to 50% with automated rollback on error-rate or latency SLO breach.
Post-rollback checklist: rotate keys, clear per-tenant buffers, run replay test harness.
